Subject: Production: p95 spike + 502s in Lumina prod VPC

Hi Marcus —

We started seeing a sharp p95 latency increase this morning on our on-prem VPC (lumina-prod-vpc) after the midnight model refresh/rollout. Baseline p95 is ~0.4s; current p95 is ~2.7s and overall throughput has dropped about 38%. We're also seeing intermittent 502s for a subset of requests.

Details:
- Observed at ~09:15 PST, steady since 09:30
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (primary) and /v1/chat (fallback)
- We attached a graph (lumina_latency_2026-11-12.png) and included a short trace sample below.

We need immediate help — this is customer-facing traffic and it's impacting scheduled workflows. Can the Redwood team run a quick mitigation and advise next steps? We can share SSH access for on-prem diagnostics if needed.

Trace snippet: trace_id=lh-6a2f0c; error=502; shard=gw-3a

Thanks,
Samantha Lee

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production: p95 spike + 502s in Lumina prod VPC

Samantha — thanks for the heads up and the trace. We're treating this as a high-priority mitigation. Immediate plan (15–45m):

1) Roll traffic to the verified fallback model: redwood-model-small-v1 (lower memory/latency profile)
2) Run KV cache warmup for the busiest prefixes on the affected nodes (gw-3a indicated in trace)
3) Temporarily increase concurrency cap on the cluster and enable burst autoscaling for +2 nodes
4) If errors persist, we'll flip request routing to the adjacent region backup (us-west-2) for a fraction of traffic and throttle long-tail batched jobs

For diagnostics we need:
- Full request/response logs for trace_id=lh-6a2f0c (timestamps +/- 2 minutes)
- Output of top-level system metrics (GPU utilization, CPU, disk I/O) for gw-3a
- Any local kubelet/kube-proxy errors if available

I've attached the latest mitigation playbook (mitigation_playbook_v2.pdf) and pinged on-call. Marissa and Laura will lead the runbook steps. Naomi, please coordinate with the infra team on the regional fallback activation.

Marcus Lin
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

On Thu, Nov 12, 2026 at 09:42 AM Samantha Lee <samantha@luminahealth.com> wrote:
> We started seeing a sharp p95 latency increase this morning on our on-prem VPC (lumina-prod-vpc) after the midnight model refresh/rollout.

Samantha — quick status: we executed the immediate mitigations Marcus listed. Actions taken so far:
- Rolled 40% of traffic to redwood-model-small-v1 (reduced p95 on that cohort to ~0.6s)
- Performed targeted KV cache warmup for the top 100 prefixes on gw-3a
- Autoscaling policy bumped by +2 nodes; warm nodes are joining but one node (gw-3a) is showing sustained GPU steal and occasional OOMk, possibly due to decoder scratch growth after the roll
- Enabled limited regional fallback for 10% of traffic to us-west-2 (observed small improvement in throughput)

We still need the full logs around trace_id=lh-6a2f0c — the request flow shows a short-lived decoder spike followed by a 502 from the local proxy. Can you run the following on your side and paste results?

1) sudo cat /var/log/redwood/proxy.err | grep "lh-6a2f0c" -n
2) kubectl -n redwood logs --since=5m --selector=shard=gw-3a --tail=200

If you prefer, we can run bundle-collect from our side if you grant temporary SSO token to the customer admin console (link below).

Temporary admin console: https://console.redwood.ai/admin/lumina-prod-vpc?token=tmpl_kJ34

We'll hold the rollbacks and observe for 2 hours; if the 502s continue on gw-3a we plan a rolling node recycle on that host tonight during the maintenance window.

Laura Bennett
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Laura — thanks, we ran the grep and gathered the traces. Attached are the logs (lumina_traces_20261113.log). Findings:
- The 502s correlate with a disk-pressure event on the node; kubelet logs show page-fault spikes and OOM notifications around 09:12–09:20
- Trace IDs: lh-6a2f0c, lh-6a2f4e, lh-6a2f9a show the same pattern across three requests

We've temporarily isolated gw-3a from the service mesh (drain) and traffic has partially recovered. We'll leave the node drained pending your team's guidance.

We're happy to give a short window of cluster admin access if you need to run additional diagnostics.

Thanks — Samantha

Date: Sun, 14 Nov 2026 17:30:00 -08:00
Subject: LuminaHealth incident — leadership summary and next steps

Team — quick leadership summary and customer ask to prepare for board-level attention from Lumina:

- What happened: Post-deploy decoder memory growth triggered disk pressure on node gw-3a in Lumina's on-prem cluster, producing intermittent 502s and p95 latency regression for a portion of traffic.
- What we did: rolled partial traffic to smaller model, warmed KV cache, bumped autoscaling, drained the bad node, and enabled a 10% regional fallback. Logs and traces shared by customer.
- Current state: partial recovery, isolated node out of rotation, customer reporting improved but not fully back to baseline.

Customer is requesting:
1) A written incident note by EOD that they can present to their CIO (include timeline and root-cause hypothesis)
2) A mitigation roadmap and a proposal for an SLA amendment (they asked about a credit if SLA breached)
3) A 9am PST war room tomorrow to finalize action items and customer communications

Action items (owners):
- Marcus: draft the incident note + timeline (target: 2 hours)
- Laura: produce a short technical RCA hypothesis and the recommended hotfix (kernel flag / decoder config) (target: 6 hours)
- Marissa: prepare the customer comms (apology + next steps + optional credit wording) and coordinate legal on SLA amendment language (target: EOD)
- Naomi: scope the regional fallback costs and confirm we can sustain 20% cross-region routing for 48 hours if needed (target: 4 hours)

If we agree to a credit we should sign off as a leadership team before any numbers are offered; preliminary thinking: up to 10% invoice credit contingent on confirmed impact window.

Samantha — we've looped leadership; Marcus will send the incident note shortly and we'll have a war room invite. Appreciate the quick isolation action on your side.

Jonas Weber
VP, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
